vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: word-comments-extractor
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle is a legitimate tool for extracting and formatting comments from Microsoft Word documents. The Python script (extract_comments.py) uses standard libraries like zipfile and xml.etree for parsing and pywin32 (Word COM interface) specifically to retrieve physical page numbers, which is a common requirement for this task. The instructions in SKILL.md are focused entirely on semantic polishing of the extracted text and do not contain any prompt injection attempts or malicious directives.

llm.summary: The skill largely does what it says (extract comments and ask the agent to polish them) but has multiple inconsistencies and some unsafe implementation details you should understand before use.

dimensions.detail: The code matches the description (unpacks .docx, extracts comments and anchor text, and uses Word COM to get page numbers). However the skill does not declare important platform/dependency requirements: it depends on pywin32 and a local Microsoft Word installation (Word COM), yet the registry metadata lists no OS restriction or required binaries. That absence is disproportionate: Word COM only works on Windows with MS Word installed.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md confines runtime behavior to local extraction and in-agent polishing (no external network calls), which matches the code. However the instructions assume the agent will open user documents with Word; opening documents with Word can execute document-side behaviors (macros, external content), and the unpack step uses zipfile.extractall which may be vulnerable to archive path-traversal if the .docx is maliciously crafted. These runtime risks are not called out in the instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with a bundled script and no install spec. The script requires the pywin32 package (mentioned in SKILL.md) and MS Word, but neither is declared in the registry requirements. Absence of an install spec means the user must manually ensure these are present; that omission is an incoherence and increases the chance of runtime surprises. No external downloads occur in the code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request any environment variables or credentials, which is proportionate for its stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled, does not request system-wide persistence, and does not modify other skills or agent-wide config. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal for skills).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to consider before installing or running this skill:

- Platform requirements: This script relies on pywin32 and uses the Word COM interface, so it only works on Windows with Microsoft Word installed. The skill metadata does not declare that requirement — confirm you can run it in an appropriate environment.

- Missing dependency and install steps: There is no install spec. You will need to install pywin32 (and ensure Python and MS Word are present). Expect runtime failure otherwise.

- Metadata inconsistencies: The included _meta.json and skill.json versions/owner IDs differ from the registry metadata (owner ID and version mismatches). That could be benign (packaging mistakes) but also suggests the published bundle wasn't consistently produced. Ask the publisher to confirm identity and versions before trusting the package.

- Document safety: The script opens the provided .docx in Word. Opening untrusted documents in Word can trigger macros or external content. Run on trusted documents only, or open inside an isolated/air-gapped Windows VM.

- Archive extraction risk: The code uses zipfile.extractall without sanitizing paths. A malicious .docx zip could contain files with traversal paths and write outside the temp directory. To be safe, validate or sanitize archive entries or run extraction in an isolated environment.

- Recommended mitigations: run the script in a disposable Windows VM or container, scan documents for macros before processing, require the publisher to provide a signed or verified source (and correct metadata), and add explicit install instructions (pywin32) and an OS restriction (Windows) to the skill metadata.

If you need higher assurance, ask the publisher to fix the metadata (owner/version), add an install spec, and harden archive extraction (safe extraction) before using on sensitive documents.
